title: Grace Days on Repayment Interest — Network Participation Agreements
content:
Under the Cascade DHMO Primary Care Dentist Agreement of the **Network Participation Agreements**, interest on a repayment of an over-recovery accrues only on the days held beyond a grace. This page sets that grace by the practice's dispute and the size of the repayment.

**Clause.** The grace of the repayment interest is set by the dispute and the size of the repayment:

- when the practice's dispute of the decided overpayment stated that the overpayment had already been refunded, there is no grace;
- when the dispute stated any other ground and the repayment is less than 100 USD, the grace is 15 days;
- otherwise the grace is not shortened by this clause.

## Terms

- **The decided overpayment** is the overpayment of the agreement's most recent dispute decision.
- **Stated ground.** This is the ground the practice gave when it filed the dispute of that overpayment, such as "already refunded" or "the claim was correctly paid".
- **The repayment** is the agreement's most recent claim payment remittance. Its amount is the principal.

## Decision table

| Ground stated in the practice's dispute | Repayment amount | Grace |
|---|---|---|
| Already refunded | Any | None (0 days) |
| Any other ground | Less than 100 USD | 15 days |
| Any other ground | 100 USD or more | Not shortened |

## Hypothetical illustrations

- A dispute stated "the claim was correctly paid", and the repayment is 99.99 USD. The grace is 15 days.
- The same dispute with a repayment of exactly 100.00 USD: the grace is not shortened.
- A dispute stated "already refunded": there is no grace, whatever the amount.
